observations: The page number «52» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01: «den 1. Jan. 1860» continues «Burgess hat nach diesen Regeln den wahren Ort des Saturns für» at the end of p. 51 (JP2 0083, L39). L16: «1. Nach Al-Battānī.», centred, the name spaced.

L17-L27: the computation, set as a table: the names joined to the figures by dotted leaders (L21-L27), which are not transcribed; in L18 the ditto marks „ stand under «Mittlere Länge» and under «nach den Tafeln»; the rows L19, L22, L24 and L27 stand below short rules under the figures; «Centrum», «Centrum aequatum», «Anomalie» and «Anomalia aequata» are indented further than the other names. Each printed row is one line here, the cells separated by our «|»; the empty cells give the columns room and are not printed.

L01-L03: Burgess's true place of Saturn for 1 January 1860, about 11° greater than the mean longitude, against about 3° by al-Khwārizmī's rules; Suter's computation is not given. L30: «20′ ∶ 60′», the colon of the ratio with a space on either side (18 and 16 px), written ∶ (U+2236). N02: «(274/68)°», the fraction built up in small figures within round brackets, the degree sign after the bracket; written {fr:274|68}.

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Kh.», «Burgess», «Batt.», «Al-Battānī»; italics: «Sūrya-Siddhānta», «Shāh», «zwei», «eine», «wahren Ortes», «Saturn», «Berechnung des wahren Ortes des Saturns». N01: «Hier ist» printed more heavily than the rest of the note (the strokes measure the same, 5 px).
The colons and semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (10-13 px measured).
